problem: Mobile manipulation needs whole-body base-arm trajectories that respect scene geometry, embodiment and task goals. Classical planners need perfect scene knowledge and hand-made goals, while learned autoregressive neural planners (MpiNets, Skill Transformer-style) are myopic and cannot eliminate physical violations.
motivation: Diffusion models generate whole trajectories and support guided sampling, but they had not been applied to high-dimensional, long-horizon mobile manipulation. Even with expert data, unguided generation still violates physical constraints, so constraints and task objectives should be enforced during generation.
key_idea: Train a scene-conditioned trajectory diffusion model on expert whole-body mobile manipulation trajectories from robot-centric 3D scans, then optimize samples at every denoising step with differentiable cost functions (collision, smoothness, joint limits) and task energy functions (grasp, place, goal-reach).
insight: Guidance is the main source of gain. Success on seen scenes goes from 21.95 to 30.54 (grasp), 4.67 to 22.89 (place) and 25.49 to 30.49 (goal-reach) when optimization is added. Ablation: pure Langevin optimization without the diffusion prior gets 0% success even at 2000 steps, while the prior with 50 steps gets 51%, so the learned prior shrinks the search space. Whole-trajectory generation also avoids the myopic jitter and end-effector non-convergence of autoregressive baselines.
method: Conditional trajectory diffusion: a DDPM-style noise-prediction network eps_theta(tau_t, t, S) generates the whole trajectory (50 steps, joint-space, 10-DoF base+arm) in one denoising process, trained with MSE on expert data.

Scene encoder: a PointTransformer encodes a robot-centric cropped point cloud (target object, scene geometry) into per-point features used as key/value in cross-attention; the trajectory embedding fused with the time embedding via ResBlock + self-attention is the query.

Guided sampling: at each denoising step the mean is shifted by Sigma_t * grad of -(energy + sum lambda_i cost_i) using a first-order Taylor approximation; the initial state is pinned to q0, and K extra refinement steps are run at the end.

Task energies: a data-driven SE(3) grasp energy (pretrained as in SE(3)-DiffusionFields) on the last configuration; a placement energy (Chamfer between object placement-surface points and target area points); a goal-reaching energy (Chamfer between end-effector points and goal points).
Physical cost functions: an SDF-based collision cost (CHOMP-style, safety margin) over robot surface points, an acceleration-based smoothness cost, and a joint-limit cost with a margin.

Expert data: whole-body trajectories from the VKC optimization planner, collected in PhyScene-generated scenes (10,673 grasp trajectories in 17 scenes and 8,996 place trajectories in 24 scenes for training/test, plus 335 and 351 held-out trajectories in unseen scenes); goal-reaching reuses the grasp data.

setting.backbone: Conditional DDPM with PointTransformer scene encoder + cross/self-attention (trained from scratch), with a pretrained SE(3) grasp energy network
setting.training_data: Expert VKC-planned whole-body trajectories in PhyScene simulated scenes: about 10.7k grasp (26 objects, 17 scenes) and about 9.0k placement (24 scenes) trajectories; goal-reaching reuses grasp trajectories; no web data
setting.observation: Robot-centric segmented/cropped 3D point cloud (scene, target object, goal/target-area points) in the initial base frame; SDF of the scene for collision cost
setting.action_space: Whole-body joint-position trajectory (3-DoF omnidirectional base + 7-DoF arm, 50 waypoints), executed by a low-level controller
setting.privileged: Perfect segmented 3D scans and scene SDF in simulation; target object/area point clouds, pre-detected placement surface; VICON localization in real world

Per-object success rates are in Table 4.
results: On the seen-scene test set, M2Diffuser reaches 30.54% (grasp), 22.89% (place) and 30.49% (goal-reach), while the strongest baselines (MpiNets/MpiFormer) stay below about 4%. In unseen scenes it reaches 14.33/12.25/12.61% against under 4% for the baselines. Optimization lowers collision rate and improves smoothness but costs 5-10x more inference time (about 4-6 s). It also transfers zero-shot from sim to a real 10-DoF Dingo+Kinova robot for pick-and-place and handover.
limitations: Slow training and inference: guidance at each denoising step rules out DDIM-style acceleration, giving about 4-6 s per trajectory.
Strong dependence on hand-designed energy and cost functions and hyperparameter tuning, impractical for multi-stage or human-like skills.
Absolute success rates are low (about 12-30%), and the collision rate stays high (20-44%), especially in unseen scenes; real-world results are qualitative with no success statistics.
builds_on: Diffuser-style planning / Motion Planning Diffusion (Huang et al.)
